[[Trongisvágur]], [[Tvøroyri]] Municipality | capacity = 4,000 (324 seated) | chairman = André Dalfoss | manager = Rasmus Nolsøe | league = [[1. deild]] | season = [[2025 Faroe Islands Premier League|2025]] | position = [[Faroe Islands Premier League]], 10th of 10 (relegated) | website = http://www.tb.fo/ | pattern_la1 = | pattern_b1 = _jomapisa2bw| pattern_ra1 = | pattern_sh1 = | leftarm1 = 000000| body1 = 000000| rightarm1 = 000000| shorts1 = 000000| socks1 = 000000| pattern_la2 =_jomaessential1819mvb| pattern_b2 = _jomaessential1819mvb | pattern_ra2 =_jomaessential1819mvb | leftarm2 = 000000| body2 = 000000| rightarm2 = 000000| shorts2 = 000000| socks2 = 000000| }} '''Tvøroyrar Bóltfelag''' is a [[Faroes]]e professional [[football (soccer)|football]] club from [[Tvøroyri]], currently playing in the second tier of Faroese football. TB Tvøroyri is the oldest football club in the [[Faroe Islands]], and also one of the oldest in the [[Danish Realm]], in which the Faroe Islands are a self-governing country. After the end of the 2016 season, it was decided on 15 December 2016 that the three clubs of the island [[Suðuroy]], which are TB Tvøroyri, [[FC Suðuroy]] and [[Royn Hvalba]] would merge into a new club for the 2017 season.{{cite web |url=http://www.nordlysid.fo/nu+verdur+eitt+felagslid+i+suduroynni+i+effodeildini.html |title=Nú verður eitt felagslið í Suðuroynni í Effodeildini |last1=Ósá |first1=Jákup |date=15 December 2016 |publisher=Norðlýsið |access-date=27 February 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170227151704/http://www.nordlysid.fo/nu+verdur+eitt+felagslid+i+suduroynni+i+effodeildini.html |archive-date=27 February 2017 }} The merger will not be complete until 2018 and the name will be all three names together for the 2017 season: [[TB/FC Suðuroy/Royn]].{{cite web |url=http://www.eurosport.com/football/teams/tb-fc-su-uroy-royn/teamcenter.shtml |title=TB/FC Suðuroy/Royn |publisher=Eurosport |access-date=27 February 2017 |archive-date=21 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221021141406/https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml |url-status=live }} The three clubs have not been dissolved yet, they continue separately for the children's and women's teams. In 2017 it will only be the men's teams which will play for the new cooperation. In Faroese the new team is referred to as ''Suðuroyarliðið'' (the Suðuroy-team).{{cite web |url=http://portal.fo/suduroyarlidid+spaeldi+soguligan+dyst+leygardagin.html |title=Suðuroyarliðið spældi søguligan dyst leygardagin |last1=Petersen |first1=Niels |date=12 February 2017 |publisher=Portal.fo |access-date=27 February 2017 |archive-date=27 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170227152345/http://portal.fo/suduroyarlidid+spaeldi+soguligan+dyst+leygardagin.html |url-status=live }} The first head coach for the Suðuroy-team is the Scottish manager [[Maurice Ross]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nordlysid.fo/norsk+innras+i+tbfc+suduroyroyn.html|title=Norsk innrás í TB/FC Suðuroy/Royn|last=Ósá|first=Jákup|date=3 February 2017|publisher=Norðlýsið|language=fo|access-date=27 February 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170227151709/http://www.nordlysid.fo/norsk+innras+i+tbfc+suduroyroyn.html|archive-date=27 February 2017}} After two years the three clubs ended the co-operation and TB Tvøroyri continued to play with their licence which was for the Faroese Premier League. In 2020 TB became a member of the [[Club of Pioneers]], a network of oldest football clubs."}}
